title: Stocks Pare AI-Driven Losses as Dip Buyers Step In: Markets Wrap
byline: SWI swissinfo ch; Bloomberg; Swissinfo API
html:
Stocks Pare AI-Driven Losses as Dip Buyers Step In: Markets Wrap

(Bloomberg) — Wild swings lashed Wall Street again, with dip buyers fading a selloff that had briefly sent the Nasdaq 100 to the brink of a bear market.

Despite mounting worries over the outlook for the artificial-intelligence trade, the tech-heavy gauge trimmed an earlier plunge to 0.6%. Nvidia Corp. sank 3.9%. In a rotation to other sectors, most S&P 500 firms rose.

Dizzying twists and turns have unsettled investors, spurring a dash for the safety of bonds ahead of a US holiday. Treasury 10-year yields fell for an eighth straight day, the longest drop since 2024.

“There is still no end in sight for the heightened volatility as investors continue to unwind leveraged risky positions, and move into bonds and other haven assets,” said Fawad Razaqzada at Stonex Trading and Forex.com.

The tech euphoria that had followed the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia’s CEO is waning. While his return soothed fears over a leadership vacuum at the heart of AI, concerns over spending and rising borrowing costs continue to fuel doubts about the sector.

Read: Fed Beige Book Shows Moderate Growth, Uptick in Wage Pressures

Inflation that has been persistently above the Federal Reserve’s 2% target is seen putting officials on track to lift rates in December.

The Fed’s preferred gauge of inflation, the personal consumption expenditures price index, rose 3.8% in October from the previous year, data released Wednesday showed.

“We are asking markets to finance one of the largest capital expenditure cycles in modern economic history, while simultaneously contemplating a monetary policy shock that makes that investment more expensive,” said Manish Singh at Crossbridge Capital. “There is an obvious contradiction.”

Singh notes that earnings expectations and valuations have adjusted. That’s not to say the downside is exhausted, but the starting point is considerably less demanding than it was few weeks ago, he added.

“All eyes on the Fed and when they walk back hawkish talk,” Singh concluded.

Corporate Highlights:

S&P Global Ratings is looking at cutting Nvidia’s credit by one notch, citing concerns over the company’s management and governance following the departure, and then the return, of its chief executive officer. Palo Alto Networks Inc., which last week announced a $4.5 billion AI acquisition, was sued by a former executive over claims he was fired for fighting back against accounting fraud at the cybersecurity company. CoreWeave Inc.’s bankers at Morgan Stanley and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group Inc. are preparing a $4.5 billion loan sale for as soon as next week, with the financing secured by graphics processing units for Meta Platforms Inc. The US Federal Communications Commission approved SpaceX’s request to launch as many as 1 million satellites for the creation of a network of data centers in orbit for complex AI computing. HP Inc. jumped after the company gave a profit forecast that will likely exceed analysts’ estimates, signaling the computer maker is improving its ability to manage rising costs associated with memory chips. Some of the main moves in markets:
